newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 17.

text.p: Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers union reached a tentative contract agreement, Ohio Edison Co agreed to buy Centerior Energy for $1.5 billion in stock, and Intel Corp said stronger-than-expected chip sales will boost profits in the coming quarter beyond analysts' views, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.
* Foundation Health and Health Systems International Inc are in merger talks.
* Bear Stearns paid its top five executives $81.3 million in cash and stock in its fiscal year ended June 30.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose 50.68 points to settle at a record-high 5889.20.
* Crude oil prices CLV6 tumbled on reports the Clinton Administration asked Saudi Arabia to boost oil production in case the latest Iraqi conflict disrupts oil shipments from the Persian Gulf.
* Business inventories rose 0.4 percent in July while sales grew by 1.2 percent.

* The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission obtained a court order freezing $950,000 in profits from options trading booked ahead of the announcement of Gillette Co's proposed merger with Duracell International Inc.
* Intuit Inc agreed to sell its electronic transaction-processing unit to CheckFree Corp for stock valued at $268 million.

* 3DO said it plans to sell all of its hardware business to concentrate on making game software for PCs and the Internet, and also said its founder was handing over operating control to the company's president.
* Two former executives at Archer Daniels Midland Co will step down as directors at the next shareholders meeting.
* Goldman Sachs reported third-quarter profit of $589 million before taxes.

* Hoping to lure more Americans away from TV by building big, glamorous "megaplex" theater complexes such as AMC Entertainment's "Grand" 24-screen theater in Dallas, movie exhibitors are embarking on an expansion binge reminiscent of specialty retailers in earlier years. - Heard on the Street.
* The bond market ended little changed, taking a breather after Friday's frenetic run-up in prices. - Credit Markets.
